exposure: surfactant via endotracheal tube during mechanical ventilation (historical control)
outcome: adverse events related to the procedure
cohort: Infants born between 2012 and 2017 with gestational age 23-36+6 weeks and a diagnosis of RDS requiring at least 30% oxygen with or without nCPAP.
finding: Transition to Minimally Invasive Surfactant Therapy (MIST) was associated with significantly reduced need for oxygen, mechanical ventilation, and surfactant, and a borderline shortened NICU admission, with no significant differences in major morbidities or mortality.
followup_time: Up to 32 days after birth (duration of NICU admission)
